extracted.intended_audience: aspiring children's and young-adult authors and picture-book author–illustrators querying literary agents
extracted.subtask_description: An individual literary agent's manuscript wish list and submission guidelines describing what kinds of children's/YA/picture-book projects she is actively seeking and how to submit them. Useful for authors preparing queries to this specific agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actively building list — middle grade priority
rubrics_metrics.description: “I’m ACTIVELY building my list right now, particularly in middle grade. If you have stellar, fun, expansive, bright, fantastical, joyful, adventurous middle grade hiding somewhere, PLEASE query me.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent is open to almost anything within middle grade; she emphasises manuscripts that are 'stellar, fun, expansive, bright, fantastical, joyful, adventurous.' She notes middle-grade readers are looking for 'fun and mischief, to learn something about life, and to escape and romp.'

rubrics_metrics.name: YA preferences — concept, voice, emotional connection
rubrics_metrics.description: “For YA, I’m eager to find novels that are high concept, diverse, fantasy or magical realism, and am open to anything conceptually unique.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also seeks YA that is 'bold and fresh with a voice that’s impossible to put aside' and that creates emotional connection: 'something that leaves me puffy eyed or laughing out loud.' She wants drama and hope; overall values the intersection between stellar writing and plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: YA sub-genre expectations — paranormal/adventure/dystopian
rubrics_metrics.description: “In the realm of paranormal, adventure, and dystopian, I’m looking for something entirely unexpected.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For these sub-genres the agent expects originality and surprises rather than trope-reliant stories; she is looking for work that subverts expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not a fit — message-driven or hard science fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: “I’m probably not the best choice for ‘message’ or hard science-fiction books.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit negative preference: authors should avoid submitting books that are primarily didactic/'message' focused or that are hard SF if they want representation from this agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture books — author/illustrator requirement and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: “With picture books, I am exclusively interested in AUTHOR/ILLUSTRATORS at this time.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: She is especially looking for 'award-worthy artwork, character-driven series, and work by diverse creators featuring diverse stories.' Submission format: attach a PDF of your dummy for picture-book submissions; links to online portfolios are welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor preference — loves funny manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: “Oh! Something else–I would love, love, LOVE to discover a FUNNY manuscript, a novel to make me LOL as Louise Rennison’s Angus, Thongs, and Full-Frontal Snogging did.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit interest in comic voice and manuscripts that make the agent laugh out loud; humor is a strong positive differentiator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity as a positive criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent lists 'diverse' among YA interests and states picture-book interest in 'work by diverse creators featuring diverse stories.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diverse voices and stories are explicitly desirable across formats (YA and picture books); diversity factors into the agent’s selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary quality criterion — intersection of stellar writing and plot
rubrics_metrics.description: “What I’m really looking for is the intersection between stellar writing and plot, something that leaves me puffy eyed or laughing out loud.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both high-quality prose/voice and compelling plotting are required; emotional impact (laughing or crying) is a strong indicator of fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission mechanics — email address and required materials
rubrics_metrics.description: “Submissions should be emailed to emily@folioliterarymanagement.com. Please send along your query letter and first ten pages of your manuscript in the body of the email.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must put QUERY in the subject line to ensure the agent sees it. If submitting a picture book, attach a PDF dummy. Links to online portfolios are welcome. The agent prefers the first ten pages in the body of the email rather than as attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response policy / assumed rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: “If you haven’t heard back from me within six weeks, I’m sorry to say I’ve decided I’m not the ideal match for your project.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectation for authors: lack of response within six weeks should be treated as a pass; agent cannot promise to respond to every query.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-level genres and favorite sub-genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of genres and sub-genres the agent represents/interested in: 'Fiction: Children's, Middle Grade, Picture Books, Young Adult' and favorites: 'Author-Illustrators, Contemporary YA, Contemporary Young Adult, Diversity, Literary Middle Grade, Middle Grade, Middle Grade Adventure, Middle Grade Contemporary, Middle Grade Fantasy, Middle Grade Humor, YA Fantasy, Young Adult, picture books.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enumerated list serves as a checklist of what the agent actively reads and is most likely to consider; authors should prioritize submitting projects that match these categories.
